site: Jezero crater floor, Mars, east of the western delta (USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE DTM)

frame.description: Local right-handed, y-up frame in meters (Three.js convention). Origin = play-area center. +x = east, +z = south, +y = up. Image columns go with +x, rows with +z; row 0 is the northern edge. Grid north is true north.
frame.projection: Azimuthal equidistant on the Mars sphere R = 3396190 m (the sphere of every input product), centered on the origin. Latitudes are planetocentric, longitudes east. Scale error < 0.001% inside the play area, < 0.1% at 100 km.
frame.toLatLon: spherical azimuthal equidistant inverse with x east, y north = -z
frame.heights: All heightmaps store TANGENT-PLANE heights: elevation above the Mars areoid (MOLA geoid, as in the source DTMs) minus the curvature drop r^2 / (2R), r = horizontal distance from the origin. The drop is 2.4 m at 4 km, 92 m at 25 km, 1.47 km at 100 km.
frame.azimuthConvention: azimuth_deg is measured from north (local -z), turning toward east (+x). Direction vector = (x: sin(az), z: -cos(az)).

sunAndEarth.note: Mars: Sun only (no Earth block). Sunset azimuth at Ls 200 is about 261 deg (solar declination -8.4 deg).

heightmap.source: USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE 1 m DTM, area-averaged to 5 m

slope.source: Computed from the 5 m heights (central differences)

softGround.formula: softness = value / 255 (0 normal ground, 1 sand ripples)
softGround.source: Seitah ripple mask (see features.softGround), softened over one pixel

distantTerrain.name: near ring
distantTerrain.hole: Covers the inner grid too; skip or sink the part inside it.
distantTerrain.source: HiRISE 1 m DTM area-averaged (12% of the ring), then the JPL CTX 20 m DEM (87%), blended over 500 m; CTX shifted -0.5 m to match HiRISE

distantTerrain.name: far ring
distantTerrain.hole: Covers the inner grid too; skip or sink the part inside it.
distantTerrain.source: JPL CTX 20 m DEM area-averaged to 200 m, then MOLA 463 m (bilinear) outside it, blended over 1 km; MOLA shifted -6.8 m to match

landing.name: Landing
landing.source: Picked by this pipeline: flattest spot 300-600 m from Perseverance's landing site, toward the delta

deltaFront.name: Delta front
deltaFront.description: Eastern front of Jezero's western delta: layered sedimentary cliffs (sandstone and mudstone laid down in the ancient lake) rising 30-60 m above the crater floor. scarpLocal_xz follows the foot of the scarp (DTM contour); samplePoint is a drivable spot at the foot.

samplePoint.name: Delta front sample
samplePoint.source: Hawksbill Gap, where Perseverance drilled the Wildcat Ridge sample (sols 490-516): Mars 2020 rover waypoints (https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/json/M20_waypoints.json)

deltaFront.source: Delta lobe fronts of Sun & Stack 2020 (USGS SIM 3464, doi:10.3133/sim3464; 100-200 m offsets to the Mars 2020 base map), Hawksbill Gap / Three Forks / Enchanted Lake rover positions (Mars 2020 rover waypoints (https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/json/M20_waypoints.json)); the line itself is the HiRISE DTM contour at the scarp foot.

footNear.name: Delta foot
footNear.description: The nearest 400 m of the delta front's scarp-foot line to the landing, with a 50 m zone around it. Blocks fallen from the delta's layers lie at the foot.
footNear.source: This pipeline: the HiRISE DTM contour at the scarp foot (deltaFront.footContour_m, on the game's 5 m heights), the part nearest the landing

floodBoulder.name: Flood boulder
floodBoulder.source: Placed by design (no such boulder was observed here); the spot is picked by this pipeline on the game's slope.png (nearest 5 m sample, as the game reads it)

seitah.name: Seitah
seitah.description: Seitah ('amidst the sand' in Navajo): olivine-rich igneous rock in NE-SW ridges, with dark sand megaripples between them. Perseverance skirted it because the sand is risky, and drove in only at its eastern edge (sols 201-340).

entryPoint.name: Seitah entry
entryPoint.source: Cheapest drivable point on the Seitah outline from the landing. Perseverance's own first look into Seitah was at 18.4327 N, 77.4413 E (sol 201; Mars 2020 rover waypoints (https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/json/M20_waypoints.json)).

seitah.source: Outline traced by this pipeline on the HiRISE DTM and orthomosaic (ridged unit below the Maaz scarp), following Farley et al. 2022 (Science 377, eabo2196, Fig. 1) and the eolian bedform areas of Sun & Stack 2020 (USGS SIM 3464); Seitah outcrops and rover path from Crumpler et al. 2023 (doi:10.1029/2022JE007444; data doi:10.5281/zenodo.7545299). Approximate (+-100 m).

softGround.description: Seitah's sand ripples as circles for the soft-ground rule (sinkage and slip), one per 150 m cell with ripples (circle area = ripple area in the cell). soft-ground.png has the same ripples at 5 m. Ripple fields outside Seitah (e.g. west of Kodiak and at the delta front) are real but left firm in the game.
softGround.source: Ripple fields detected by this pipeline in the HiRISE 25 cm orthomosaic (oriented texture of megaripple crests, cached at 2.5 m), plus the ripples mapped along Perseverance's traverse by Crumpler et al. 2023 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7545299, CC BY 4.0)

rockyAreas.name: Rocky area 1
rockyAreas.source: Crumpler et al. 2023, Crater Ejecta Blocks layer (107 mapped blocks; doi:10.5281/zenodo.7545299)
rockyAreas.description: Field of ejecta blocks around a small crater just south of Perseverance's landing site. Scatter boulders densest here.

rockyAreas.name: Rocky area 2
rockyAreas.source: Picked by this pipeline on the HiRISE DTM: the sharpest small crater on the floor away from the other sites (fresh craters on the Jezero floor carry blocky ejecta in HiRISE images)
rockyAreas.description: Crater about 340 m across (310 to 450 m by direction) and 16 m deep, an older crater; its rim is lowest on the south side. Its inner wall is steepest (26 deg) on the north-west side and most rim blocks are on the north-west side; scatter boulders on its rim. Its inner wall may be too steep to drive.

viewpoints.name: Delta viewpoint
viewpoints.source: Picked by this pipeline on the HiRISE DTM: crater-floor spot facing the delta front (Sun & Stack 2020 delta lobe front; Mars 2020 delta-front campaign area)
viewpoints.note: The scarp rises 48 m, 17.5 deg above the horizontal from here.

viewpoints.name: West viewpoint
viewpoints.source: Picked by this pipeline on the HiRISE DTM: high drivable ground on the delta with the lowest horizon toward the sunset
viewpoints.note: Faces azimuth 261 deg (sunset at Ls 200); the horizon there (the western crater rim) is 4.8 deg high.

perseveranceLanding.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
perseveranceLanding.source: Mars 2020 rover waypoints (https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/json/M20_waypoints.json), sol 13 position; NASA gives 18.4447 N, 77.4508 E

notes: Drive distances are least-cost routes on a 10 m grid avoiding slopes over 18 deg; straight-line distances are also given.
Names are ASCII; display names (Seitah with accents, etc.) live in the game's text data.
The landing is near Perseverance's 2021 landing site but not on it; the real site is features.perseveranceLanding.
Seitah's outline is approximate (+-100 m): no machine-readable map of the unit exists, so it was traced on the HiRISE data following published maps.
Soft ground is limited to Seitah's ripples (inside its outline plus 150 m); the ripple detection is automatic and may miss small ripple patches or include some finely layered rock.

Mars sites features (youngCraters, slopeTargets, deltaFront.footNear, deltaFront.floodBoulder, perseveranceSites, missionLandmarks) come from game/tools/mars_sites.py, for Chieri's review. They read the game's own 5 m heights and slope.png, so a features-only run gives the same lists.

youngCraters: rim crest fitted per direction on the 5 m heights; 80 to 400 m across, depth >= 2.5 m and >= 0.015 x diameter, crest on >= 75% of directions, center within 1600 m. freshness 'fresh': round (90th/10th percentile crest radius <= 1.5) and boulder shadows (compact blobs darker than 0.6 x the local mean, 0.25 to 8 m^2, in the 25 cm HiRISE mosaic) on the rim (0.8-1.2 R) at >= 20/ha and >= 3 x the 2.5-3.5 R ring, and a raised rim (rimUplift_m >= 2). Every crater here has a sand-filled floor and none keeps a blocky ejecta blanket beyond its rim: 'fresh' means a sharp, round, blocky rim. driveDistanceFromLanding_m and drivePoint are for the cheapest rim cell; floorDriveDistance_m is to the center (null if the floor cannot be reached under 18 deg).

slopeTargets: 5 m cells at 10-18 deg in slope.png with a 4-neighbour under 8 deg, reachable and off the ripples, grouped (8-connected) per site: young craters (rim radius + 40 m), the two knobs (100 m) and the delta foot zone; a cell belongs to its nearest site. The 4 largest patches per site are listed; local is the target cell nearest the patch center (cells x 25 m^2 is its area), levelCell its level neighbour, and driveDistanceFromLanding_m the route to that level cell.

deltaFront.footNear: the nearest 400 m of the scarp-foot contour, 50 m zone. deltaFront.floodBoulder is placed by design: a spot on the lower scarp slope where a 2.5 m boulder has 12-18 deg ground on its uphill and side faces and ground under 10 deg within 3 m of its downhill face (readingSpot), outside 1350 m from the landing.

perseveranceSites: rocks Perseverance abraded and sampled within 1600 m, at the rover's end-of-drive waypoint for the sample sol (roverStayedSols: from that waypoint until it next moved). Names, sols and dates are from NASA's sample list and must be fact-checked again before they reach game text.

missionLandmarks: Wright Brothers Field from the waypoints (approximate). The Mars 2020 backshell, parachute and descent stage are not placed: their positions need sources this pipeline does not use (HiRISE images or the Ingenuity flight log).

perseveranceSites.source: Mars 2020 rover waypoints (https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/json/M20_waypoints.json); sample names, sols and dates: NASA (https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-2020-perseverance/mars-rock-samples/)

missionLandmarks.name: Wright Brothers Field
missionLandmarks.note: The rover's position on sol 43 (April 3, 2021), when it set Ingenuity down on the airfield from beneath its belly; Ingenuity's first flights took off within a few meters of here. Approximate (+-10 m): not from the Ingenuity flight log.

horizonFromLanding.note: Index = azimuth in degrees (see frame.azimuthConvention). Includes curvature.
